vedic_reference.root_origin: Tamil Mythology, Murugan is a major deity in the Hindu pantheon, and one of the most popular gods in Tamil Nadu
vedic_reference.note: Murugan is considered an incarnation of Lord Shiva and is also known as Kartikeya, the god of war, and Skanda, the god of auspiciousness. He is often depicted as a youthful, handsome, and powerful god, holding a spear, a drum, and a flag.

data.cultural_impact: The name Muruganraj holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism as it is a devotional title carried by those who hold deep reverence for Lord Murugan. Lord Murugan, also known as Shanmukha or Kartikeya, is the god of love, war, and fertility, the younger son of Shiva and Parvati. Adored primarily in the southernmost Indian states and Sri Lanka, Murugan is depicted as carrying a spear, an awkward Vel, a drum, and a peacock feather in each of his hands. Worship of Murugan is particularly prevalent in the Tamil language area. Commemorations of his birth and taking of the Vel are prominent during the month of Arayathruthazhadi in the Tamil calendar. The name Muruganraj could inspire a deep devotion towards Lord Murugan and promote a connection to the rich cultural heritage and traditions of Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Muruganraj attains significant spiritual significance through its allusion to Lord Murugan. In Hinduism, divinity is a central concept, and the names and titles of deities hold a deeper meaning. Murugan, as a god, embodies love, war, and fertility, representing the dynamic and complex aspects of life. Through this name, one can strive to foster a sense of love, compassion, courage, and creativity, leading a virtuous and fulfilling life. The name Muruganraj serves as both a personal reminder and a spiritual inspiration to lead a compassionate and brave life, offering guidance and protecting us in the face of life's challenges, just like Lord Murugan.

historical_references.reference: Muruganraj was the name of a great Chola king who ruled from around 1050-1070 AD. He is known for extending the Chola empire in the south and strengthening its power base.

Muruganraj is also the name of a renowned 16th century Tamil poet and scholar, who contributed significantly to the Tamil literature. He is believed to have composed several works on various subjects, including love, war, and religion.
